theorem_title: Rational perturbation bound for the pair Hessian residual
formal_statement:
theorem HlawkaSchatten.DiagonalCutoff21.residual_energy_bound_rounded {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (rho S : ℝ) (a b : ι → ℝ)
    (hrho : 0 ≤ rho) (hS : 0 ≤ S)
    (ha : ∑ i, (a i) ^ 2 ≤ 3 * S)
    (hb : ∑ i, (b i) ^ 2 ≤ 4 * rho ^ 2 * S) :
    ∑ i, (a i - b i) ^ 2 ≤ (7 / 4 + 2 * rho) ^ 2 * S := by sorry
natural_language_statement: For any finite index type $\iota$, real numbers $\rho,S\ge0$, and real families $a_i,b_i$ indexed by $\iota$, suppose $\sum_i a_i^2\le3S$ and $\sum_i b_i^2\le4\rho^2 S$. Then $\sum_i(a_i-b_i)^2\le(7/4+2\rho)^2S$. The assertion includes the empty index type, zero residuals and $\rho=0$. It is the algebraic energy estimate used after the two operator bounds in the pair-residual argument.

import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Ring.Finset
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring
import Mathlib.Tactic.Positivity

formal_statement:
theorem HlawkaSchatten.DiagonalCutoff21.matrix_pair_residual_bound_explicit (U : Fin 3 → Fin 3 → ℝ)
    (theta : Fin 6 → ℝ) (rho : ℝ) (hrho : 0 ≤ rho)
    (htheta : ∀ i, |theta i| ≤ rho) :
    ∑ i, ((![U 1 1 + U 2 1, U 1 2 + U 2 2, U 0 0 + U 2 0, U 0 2 + U 2 2, U 0 0 + U 1 0, U 0 1 + U 1 1] : Fin 6 → ℝ) i - theta i * (![U 1 0 + U 2 0, U 1 0 + U 2 0, U 0 1 + U 2 1, U 0 1 + U 2 1, U 0 2 + U 1 2, U 0 2 + U 1 2] : Fin 6 → ℝ) i) ^ 2 ≤

Let $U$ be any real $3\times3$ matrix, let $\rho\ge0$, and let six real coefficients $\theta_{ki}$ satisfy $|\theta_{ki}|\le\rho$, indexed by $k,i\in\{0,1,2\}$ with $i\ne k$. If $\{j,r,k\}=\{0,1,2\}$, set $e_{ki}=U_{ji}+U_{ri}-\theta_{ki}(U_{jk}+U_{rk})$. Then

$$\sum_{k=0}^2\sum_{i\ne k}e_{ki}^2\le(7/4+2\rho)^2\sum_{j=0}^2\sum_{i=0}^2 U_{ji}^2.$$

This controls the non-radial error in the pair Hessian bound. It requires no orthogonality condition on $U$.

The proved weighted-square estimate then yields the claimed rational coefficient. Every helper proof is included in the submitted file.

theorem_title: Cyclic Hlawka constant at most p/2 throughout [21,32]
formal_statement:
theorem HlawkaSchatten.DiagonalCutoff21.cyclicConstant_upper21 {p : ℝ} (hp : 21 ≤ p) (hp32 : p ≤ 32) :
    cyclicConstant p ≤ p/2 := by sorry
preamble:
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.SpecificFunctions.Basic
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.NormNum
import Mathlib.Tactic.Positivity
import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring
import Definitions.Def_HlawkaSchatten_DiagonalConstruction_Cyclic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.ExponentialBounds
open HlawkaSchatten.DiagonalConstruction
natural_language_statement:
Let $p$ be any real exponent with $21\le p\le32$. Define

$$A_p(t)=(t^p+2)^{1/p},\qquad B_p(t)=(2|1-t|^p+2^p)^{1/p},$$
$$R_p(t)=\frac{3A_p(t)-3^{1/p}|2-t|}{6A_p(t)-3B_p(t)},\qquad K_p=\sup_{1/2\le t\le2}R_p(t).$$

Then $K_p\le p/2$. The exponent ranges over the entire real interval. This is the upper-bound component of both scalar-window milestones in the source paper.
source: Yuxuan Xu, A computer-assisted sharp diagonal Hlawka inequality for real exponents p >= 21, v1 (2026), https://github.com/Anchen-AI4Math/hlawka-diagonal-certificates/blob/main/paper/main.pdf . Section 2, equation (7), upper-bound component; elementary analytic proof in formalization/Hlawka21/CyclicUpper.lean.
explanation: Put a=3^(1/p) and b=2^(1/p). Logarithm and exponential bounds give a>=1+1/p, a<=3, 1+.69/p+.69^2/(2p^2)<=b<=1+1/p. Bernoulli and the proved two-tail estimate give Bp(t)<=2+10^-5. Since Ap(t)>=max(b,t), the quantity 2(p-1)Ap(t)+(2/3)a(2-t) is at least 2p+10^-3 for p>=21. On p<=32 this dominates p Bp(t). The denominator is positive from Ap(t)>=1+1/64, so rearranging proves Rp(t)<=p/2, and taking the supremum closes the result. The complete file proves all helpers and imports no open theorem.

theorem_title: Envelope strictly below the linear threshold for all real p >= 21
formal_statement:
theorem HlawkaSchatten.DiagonalCutoff21.envelope_linear21 {p : ℝ} (hp : 21 ≤ p) :
    scalarEnvelope p (1011/2500 : ℝ) < (273/625 : ℝ)*p := by sorry
preamble:
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.SpecificFunctions.Basic
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.NormNum
import Mathlib.Tactic.Positivity
import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring
import Definitions.Def_HlawkaSchatten_DiagonalConstruction_ScalarBounds
open HlawkaSchatten.DiagonalConstruction
natural_language_statement:
For any real $p\ge21$, define

$$E_p(q)=\frac{1-q}{2(1-((1+q^p)/2)^{1/p})}.$$

At $q=1011/2500$ and $c=273/625$ one has $E_p(q)<cp$. The assertion includes all real exponents above the endpoint, without an upper endpoint restriction. Together with the source paper's cyclic lower bound $cp<K_p$, it implies the required envelope comparison.
source: Yuxuan Xu, A computer-assisted sharp diagonal Hlawka inequality for real exponents p >= 21, v1 (2026), https://github.com/Anchen-AI4Math/hlawka-diagonal-certificates/blob/main/paper/main.pdf . Section 2, equation (7), envelope comparison parameters in Table 1. This stronger linear comparison is proved by a rational endpoint certificate and Bernoulli scaling in formalization/Hlawka21/Envelope.lean.
explanation: Let m be the endpoint and d=(1-q)/(2c). An exact rational integer-power computation gives (1+q^m)/2<(1-d/m)^m. Since 0<=q<1, q^p<=q^m for every real p>=m. Bernoulli applied with exponent p/m proves (1-d/m)^m<=(1-d/p)^p. Taking positive p-th roots yields ((1+q^p)/2)^(1/p)<1-d/p. Its denominator is positive, so rearranging gives E_p(q)<cp. All endpoint computations and scaling steps are proved in the submitted Lean file.
